diff --git a/bandit/core/nosec.py b/bandit/core/nosec.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..42abf8d
--- /dev/null
+++ b/bandit/core/nosec.py
@@ -0,0 +1,413 @@
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Parsing of the ``# nosec`` comments and directives.
+
+Three kinds of suppression comments are understood:
+
+``# nosec [TESTS]``
+    suppresses findings for the statement the comment belongs to.
+``# nosec-begin [SELECTOR]`` ... ``# nosec-end``
+    suppresses findings for a region of code.
+``# nosec-next-line [SELECTOR]``
+    suppresses findings for the statement following the comment.
+
+The directive keywords are matched case insensitively and take an optional
+selector naming the tests to suppress. Suppressions are collected into a
+mapping of line number to the set of test IDs suppressed for that line, where
+an empty set means "every test", a blanket suppression.
+"""
+import fnmatch
+import io
+import logging
+import re
+import tokenize
+
+from bandit.core import extension_loader
+from bandit.core import utils
+
+LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+#: A suppression that applies to every test rather than to named tests.
+BLANKET = frozenset()
+
+# A plain "# nosec" comment. The lookahead keeps it from swallowing the
+# directives below, which are handled separately.
+NOSEC_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s*nosec(?!-)\:?\s*(?P<tests>[^#]+)?#?")
+NOSEC_COMMENT_TESTS = re.compile(r"(?:(B\d+|[a-z\d_]+),?)+", re.IGNORECASE)
+
+BEGIN_DIRECTIVE = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-begin\b:?(?P<selector>[^#]*)", re.IGNORECASE
+)
+END_DIRECTIVE = re.compile(r"#\s*nosec-end\b", re.IGNORECASE)
+NEXT_LINE_DIRECTIVE = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-next-line\b:?(?P<selector>[^#]*)", re.IGNORECASE
+)
+
+# Lines skipped while looking for the statement a "# nosec-next-line"
+# directive applies to, once any comment has been removed from them.
+FILLER_LINE = re.compile(r"(?:[()\[\]{};]|\.\.\.)*")
+
+# Tokens of a selector expression. Whitespace and commas separate tokens
+# that are unioned together.
+SELECTOR_TOKEN = re.compile(
+    r"(?P<separator>[\s,]+)|(?P<operator>[()|&!-])|(?P<name>[A-Za-z0-9_*?]+)"
+)
+SELECTOR_OPERATORS = frozenset("()|&!-")
+
+_BEGIN = "begin"
+_END = "end"
+_NEXT_LINE = "next-line"
+
+# Token types that never start a statement.
+_NON_CODE_TOKENS = frozenset(
+    (
+        tokenize.NL,
+        tokenize.INDENT,
+        tokenize.DEDENT,
+        tokenize.ENDMARKER,
+    )
+)
+
+
+class SelectorError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a selector expression cannot be parsed."""
+
+
+def scan(data):
+    """Collect the comments and the statements of a source file.
+
+    :param data: the raw contents of the file
+    :return: a tuple of the decoded lines of the file, a dict of line number
+             -> (column, comment) and a dict mapping the first line of every
+             statement to its last line
+    """
+    encoding = "utf-8"
+    comments = dict()
+    statements = dict()
+    start = None
+    try:
+        tokens = tokenize.tokenize(io.BytesIO(data).readline)
+        for token in tokens:
+            if token.type == tokenize.ENCODING:
+                encoding = token.string
+            elif token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
+                comments[token.start[0]] = (token.start[1], token.string)
+            elif token.type == tokenize.NEWLINE:
+                if start is not None:
+                    statements[start] = token.start[0]
+                    start = None
+            elif token.type not in _NON_CODE_TOKENS and start is None:
+                start = token.start[0]
+    except tokenize.TokenError:
+        # the file could only be partly tokenized, keep what was found
+        pass
+
+    lines = data.decode(encoding, errors="replace").splitlines()
+    return lines, comments, statements
+
+
+def parse_nosec_comment(comment):
+    """Get the tests suppressed by a plain "# nosec" comment.
+
+    :param comment: the text of the comment
+    :return: ``None`` when the comment is not a nosec comment, an empty set
+             for a blanket suppression or the set of test IDs to suppress
+    """
+    found_no_sec_comment = NOSEC_COMMENT.search(comment)
+    if not found_no_sec_comment:
+        # there was no nosec comment
+        return None
+
+    matches = found_no_sec_comment.groupdict()
+    nosec_tests = matches.get("tests", set())
+
+    # empty set indicates that there was a nosec comment without specific
+    # test ids or names
+    test_ids = set()
+    if nosec_tests:
+        extman = extension_loader.MANAGER
+        # lookup tests by short code or name
+        for test in NOSEC_COMMENT_TESTS.finditer(nosec_tests):
+            test_match = test.group(1)
+            test_id = find_test_id(extman, test_match)
+            if test_id:
+                test_ids.add(test_id)
+
+    return test_ids
+
+
+def parse_directives(lines, comments, statements, tests):
+    """Get the tests suppressed by the nosec directives of a file.
+
+    :param lines: the decoded lines of the file
+    :param comments: dict of line number -> (column, comment)
+    :param statements: dict of statement start line -> statement end line
+    :param tests: the set of test IDs enabled for the current run
+    :return: a dict of line number -> set of tests to suppress for the line,
+             where an empty set suppresses every test
+    """
+    directives = _find_directives(comments, tests)
+    if not directives:
+        return dict()
+
+    suppressed = dict()
+    # regions are (indentation, tests) tuples, innermost region last
+    regions = []
+    for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
+        indent = _indentation(line)
+        if indent is not None:
+            # a region opened on an indented line ends where that block does
+            while regions and indent < regions[-1][0]:
+                regions.pop()
+
+        kind, selected = directives.get(lineno, (None, None))
+        if kind == _END and regions:
+            regions.pop()
+
+        # the line a region begins on is not part of it, an enclosing region
+        # or an earlier "# nosec-next-line" may still suppress it
+        for _, region_tests in regions:
+            _suppress(suppressed, lineno, region_tests)
+
+        if kind == _BEGIN:
+            regions.append((indent, selected))
+        elif kind == _NEXT_LINE:
+            for target in _next_statement(lineno, lines, comments, statements):
+                _suppress(suppressed, target, selected)
+
+    return suppressed
+
+
+def resolve_selector(selector, tests):
+    """Get the tests selected by the argument of a nosec directive.
+
+    :param selector: the selector expression, possibly empty
+    :param tests: the set of test IDs enabled for the current run
+    :return: ``None`` when nothing is suppressed, an empty set for a blanket
+             suppression or the set of test IDs to suppress
+    """
+    selector = selector.strip()
+    if not selector:
+        return BLANKET
+
+    try:
+        resolved = _SelectorParser(selector, tests).parse()
+    except SelectorError as e:
+        LOG.warning(
+            "Selector in comment: %s could not be parsed (%s), "
+            "falling back to a union of its tokens",
+            selector,
+            e,
+        )
+        resolved = _union_of_tokens(selector, tests)
+
+    resolved &= tests
+    if not resolved:
+        return None
+    # a selector covering every enabled test is a blanket suppression
+    return BLANKET if resolved == tests else resolved
+
+
+def find_test_id(extman, name):
+    """Get the ID of the test a nosec comment refers to.
+
+    :param extman: the extension manager holding the known tests
+    :param name: a test ID or test name
+    :return: the test ID, or ``None`` if the name is unknown
+    """
+    if extman.check_id(name):
+        return name
+    # Finding by short_id didn't work, let's check the test name
+    test_id = extman.get_test_id(name)
+    if not test_id:
+        # Name and short id didn't work:
+        LOG.warning(
+            "Test in comment: %s is not a test name or id, ignoring", name
+        )
+    return test_id  # We want to return None or the string here regardless
+
+
+def _find_directives(comments, tests):
+    """Get the directive of every comment holding one.
+
+    :param comments: dict of line number -> (column, comment)
+    :param tests: the set of test IDs enabled for the current run
+    :return: a dict of line number -> (kind, selected tests)
+    """
+    directives = dict()
+    for lineno, (_, comment) in comments.items():
+        match = NEXT_LINE_DIRECTIVE.search(comment)
+        if match:
+            selected = resolve_selector(match.group("selector"), tests)
+            directives[lineno] = (_NEXT_LINE, selected)
+            continue
+
+        match = BEGIN_DIRECTIVE.search(comment)
+        if match:
+            selected = resolve_selector(match.group("selector"), tests)
+            directives[lineno] = (_BEGIN, selected)
+            continue
+
+        # anything trailing a "# nosec-end" is ignored
+        if END_DIRECTIVE.search(comment):
+            directives[lineno] = (_END, None)
+
+    return directives
+
+
+def _next_statement(lineno, lines, comments, statements):
+    """Get the lines of the statement a directive on ``lineno`` applies to.
+
+    Blank lines, comments and lines made up of grouping tokens only are
+    skipped while looking for that statement.
+    """
+    for target in range(lineno + 1, len(lines) + 1):
+        comment = comments.get(target)
+        code = lines[target - 1]
+        if comment is not None:
+            code = code[: comment[0]]
+        if FILLER_LINE.fullmatch(code.strip()):
+            continue
+        return range(target, _statement_end(target, statements) + 1)
+    return range(0)
+
+
+def _statement_end(lineno, statements):
+    """Get the last line of the statement covering ``lineno``."""
+    for start, end in statements.items():
+        if start <= lineno <= end:
+            return end
+    return lineno
+
+
+def _indentation(line):
+    """Get the width of the leading whitespace of a line, if it has code."""
+    stripped = line.strip()
+    if not stripped:
+        return None
+    return len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
+
+
+def _suppress(suppressed, lineno, tests):
+    """Add the tests suppressed by a directive to a line."""
+    if tests is None:
+        return
+    suppressed[lineno] = utils.merge_nosec(suppressed.get(lineno), tests)
+
+
+def _resolve_token(token, tests):
+    """Get the tests a single selector token refers to."""
+    keyword = token.lower()
+    if keyword == "all":
+        return set(tests)
+    if keyword == "none":
+        return set()
+
+    if "*" in token or "?" in token:
+        # test IDs are upper case, a glob matches them by prefix
+        pattern = token.upper()
+        matched = {t for t in tests if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(t, pattern)}
+        if not matched:
+            LOG.warning(
+                "Test in comment: %s does not match any test id, ignoring",
+                token,
+            )
+        return matched
+
+    test_id = find_test_id(extension_loader.MANAGER, token)
+    return {test_id} if test_id else set()
+
+
+def _union_of_tokens(selector, tests):
+    """Resolve a selector that does not parse as a union of its tokens."""
+    resolved = set()
+    for token in re.split(r"[\s,]+", selector):
+        if token:
+            resolved |= _resolve_token(token, tests)
+    return resolved
+
+
+class _SelectorParser:
+    """Recursive descent parser for the selector of a nosec directive.
+
+    ``!`` binds tightest, followed by ``&``, then ``-`` and finally ``|``,
+    which matches the precedence of the equivalent Python set operators.
+    Tokens that merely follow each other are unioned.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, selector, tests):
+        self.tokens = self._tokenize(selector)
+        self.tests = tests
+        self.pos = 0
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _tokenize(selector):
+        tokens = []
+        pos = 0
+        while pos < len(selector):
+            match = SELECTOR_TOKEN.match(selector, pos)
+            if match is None:
+                raise SelectorError(f"unexpected {selector[pos]!r}")
+            if match.lastgroup != "separator":
+                tokens.append(match.group())
+            pos = match.end()
+        return tokens
+
+    def parse(self):
+        value = self._union()
+        if self.pos != len(self.tokens):
+            raise SelectorError(f"unexpected {self.tokens[self.pos]!r}")
+        return value
+
+    def _peek(self):
+        return self.tokens[self.pos] if self.pos < len(self.tokens) else None
+
+    def _accept(self, token):
+        if self._peek() == token:
+            self.pos += 1
+            return True
+        return False
+
+    def _starts_operand(self):
+        token = self._peek()
+        if token is None:
+            return False
+        return token in ("(", "!") or token not in SELECTOR_OPERATORS
+
+    def _union(self):
+        value = self._difference()
+        while self._accept("|") or self._starts_operand():
+            value = value | self._difference()
+        return value
+
+    def _difference(self):
+        value = self._intersection()
+        while self._accept("-"):
+            value = value - self._intersection()
+        return value
+
+    def _intersection(self):
+        value = self._unary()
+        while self._accept("&"):
+            value = value & self._unary()
+        return value
+
+    def _unary(self):
+        if self._accept("!"):
+            return set(self.tests) - self._unary()
+        return self._primary()
+
+    def _primary(self):
+        token = self._peek()
+        if token is None:
+            raise SelectorError("selector ended unexpectedly")
+        self.pos += 1
+
+        if token == "(":
+            value = self._union()
+            if not self._accept(")"):
+                raise SelectorError("missing closing parenthesis")
+            return value
+        if token in SELECTOR_OPERATORS:
+            raise SelectorError(f"unexpected {token!r}")
+        return _resolve_token(token, self.tests)

+def merge_nosec(first, second):
+    """Combine two sets of tests suppressed by nosec comments.
+
+    ``None`` means that nothing is suppressed while an empty set is a blanket
+    suppression of every test, which takes precedence over a set naming
